name: pinneapple_twin3d

children.name: pinneapple_twin3d.demo
children.doc:
Demo scene: a 90-degree pipe bend with erosion wear growing over time, plus two sensors.

Mirrors the PINNeAPPle-CFD v1 case (bend with sand, wear concentrated on the outer wall of the
bend). The wear field here is a smooth *illustrative* pattern, not a CFD result: use it to try the
viewer, then replace it with the fields of a real run.

    from pinneapple_twin3d.demo import pipe_bend_scene
    pipe_bend_scene().export("out/bend"); serve("out/bend")
children.summary: Demo scene: a 90-degree pipe bend with erosion wear growing over time, plus two sensors.

children.name: pinneapple_twin3d.gallery
children.doc:
Gallery: 3D twins of very different parts built from primitives, to exercise the generator beyond liners.

    from pinneapple_twin3d import gallery
    gallery.export_all("out/gallery")         # one folder per part + index.html
    gallery.get("rocket").export("out/rocket")

Parts: runner channel (blast-furnace trough), mixing tank, oil pipeline, airliner, launch vehicle, quadcopter drone,
lunar rover, wind turbine, satellite.

**Every field here is ILLUSTRATIVE** (simple closed-form patterns in space and time that place the physics where
an engineer expects it: stagnation heating at a nose, erosion at a bend, ...). They are not simulation or measurement
results, and each scene's title and ``source`` say so. Swap in real fields with ``Scene.add_field``.

functions.name: runner_channel
functions.doc: Blast-furnace cast-house runner: refractory-lined U trough from the tap hole to the skimmer.

functions.name: mixing_tank
functions.doc: Agitated tank: dished bottom, baffles, two-stage pitched-blade impeller; tracer blending over time.

functions.name: oil_pipeline
functions.doc: Buried-style crude line with two bends and a sag: wall loss from corrosion/erosion over 20 years.

functions.name: airliner
functions.doc: Narrow-body airliner: fuselage, swept wing, tail, two engines; skin temperature and wing-root load over a flight.

functions.name: rocket
functions.doc: Launch vehicle: ogive nose, tank stack, bell nozzle, four fins; aero heating and nozzle ablation during ascent.

functions.name: drone
functions.doc: Quadcopter: body, arms, motors, rotor discs, battery; motor and battery heating over a 20-minute flight.

functions.name: lunar_rover
functions.doc: Six-wheel lunar rover over one lunar day-night cycle: chassis temperature and regolith wheel wear.

functions.name: wind_turbine
functions.doc: Three-blade turbine: tapered tower, nacelle, twisted blades; leading-edge erosion and fatigue over 20 years.

functions.name: satellite
functions.doc: Small satellite in LEO: bus, two solar wings, dish; thermal cycling through sunlight and eclipse.

functions.name: export_all
functions.doc: Export every gallery part to ``folder/<key>/`` and write ``folder/index.html`` linking them.

children.summary: Gallery: 3D twins of very different parts built from primitives, to exercise the generator beyond liners.

children.name: pinneapple_twin3d.library
children.doc:
The geometry library from the twin side: ``pinneapple_twin3d.library.build("viper_rover").scene()``.

Alias of :mod:`pinneapple_design.geometry_library` (``pp.geometries``); a library geometry becomes a twin part
with ``Scene.add_part(name, *geom.mesh())``.
children.summary: The geometry library from the twin side: pinneapple_twin3d.library.build("viper_rover").scene().

children.name: pinneapple_twin3d.openfoam
children.doc:
OpenFOAM case -> Twin3D scene: wall patches as surfaces, per-face values over time.

Built for the PINNeAPPle-CFD erosion maps (erosion rate per wall face, possibly at several
times), but generic: any per-face quantity keyed by the global OpenFOAM face id, or boundary
fields read from the case's time directories.

    from pinneapple_twin3d.openfoam import scene_from_case
    sc = scene_from_case("case/", face_values={"erosion_rate": {1057: 0.8, 1058: 1.3}},
                         units={"erosion_rate": "mm/year"})
    sc.export("out/twin")

Faces keep their own value (vertices are duplicated per face, fan-triangulated), so a per-face
map is shown exactly as computed, with no smoothing across faces. ASCII and binary polyMesh
files are both read (binary through ``pinneapple_simulation.external_solvers.openfoam``).

functions.name: read_boundary
functions.doc: ``{patch: {"type": str, "startFace": int, "nFaces": int}}`` in file order.

functions.name: read_boundary_field
functions.sig: (path: str, patch: str, n_faces: int) -> Optional[np.ndarray]
functions.doc: Per-face values of ``patch`` in a volScalarField/volVectorField file (vectors -> magnitude).

functions.name: scene_from_case
functions.sig: (case: str, *, title: Optional[str] = None, patches: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None, face_values: Optional[Dict[str, FaceValues]] = None, units: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None, boundary_fields: Sequence[str] = (), times: Optional[Sequence[float]] = None, time_unit: str = 's', fill: float = 0.0, length_unit: str = 'm', source: str = '') -> Scene
functions.doc:
Build a Twin3D scene from an OpenFOAM case.

Parameters
----------
patches : patch names to show; default = every ``wall`` patch.
face_values : ``{field: values}`` keyed by *global* face id. ``values`` is a mapping
    ``{face_id: value}`` (one instant), a sequence of such mappings (one per time step), or an
    array of shape (n_faces_total,) / (T, n_faces_total). Faces without a value get ``fill``.
boundary_fields : field names read from every time directory (patch values; vectors -> |v|).
times : time values for the steps of ``face_values`` (default: 0..T-1); ignored when only
    ``boundary_fields`` are given (then the case's time directories are used).

children.summary: OpenFOAM case -> Twin3D scene: wall patches as surfaces, per-face values over time.

children.name: pinneapple_twin3d.primitives
children.doc:
Mesh primitives for building twin parts without a CAD file: revolve, sweep, loft, box, cylinder.

Every function returns ``(vertices (V, 3) float, faces (F, 3) int)`` with y up, in metres. Vertices are shared
within a primitive (smooth shading); combine primitives with :func:`merge`. Winding is consistent but the exported
glTF material is double sided, so orientation never hides a face.

functions.name: revolve
functions.sig: (profile: Sequence[Tuple[float, float]], n_theta: int = 48, *, cap: bool = False) -> Mesh
functions.doc: Surface of revolution of ``(r, y)`` points around the y axis (``cap`` closes the ends with a fan).

functions.name: sweep
functions.sig: (section: Sequence[Tuple[float, float]], path: Sequence[Sequence[float]], *, closed: bool = True, up: Sequence[float] = (0, 1, 0)) -> Mesh
functions.doc:
Extrude a 2D section ``(u, v)`` along a 3D path. ``u`` runs along the frame normal (closest to ``up``),
``v`` along the binormal. ``closed=False`` leaves an open profile (e.g. a U-channel).

functions.name: airfoil
functions.sig: (chord: float = 1.0, thickness: float = 0.12, n: int = 24) -> np.ndarray
functions.doc: Closed symmetric NACA 00xx outline, ``(2n, 2)``: x along the chord from the leading edge, y thickness.

functions.name: loft
functions.doc: Skin through rings of equal point count ``(K, 3)`` (closed rings): wings, blades, fuselage sections.

functions.name: wing
functions.sig: (span: float, root_chord: float, tip_chord: float, *, sweep_deg: float = 0.0, dihedral_deg: float = 0.0, twist_deg: float = 0.0, thickness: float = 0.12, n_sections: int = 12, n_pts: int = 20) -> Mesh
functions.doc: Half wing / blade along +z from the root (z=0): chord along x (leading edge at -x), thickness along y.

functions.name: cylinder
functions.sig: (p0: Sequence[float], p1: Sequence[float], radius: float, n_theta: int = 32, *, cap: bool = True) -> Mesh
functions.doc: Cylinder between two points (``radius`` may be a pair for a frustum).

functions.name: transform
functions.sig: (mesh: Mesh, *, R: np.ndarray | None = None, t: Sequence[float] = (0, 0, 0), scale: float = 1.0) -> Mesh

functions.name: mesh_quality
functions.doc: Sanity numbers used by the tests: finite coordinates, indices in range, degenerate-triangle share, bounds.

children.name: pinneapple_twin3d.scan
children.doc:
Twin geometry from scans: cleaned scan meshes and MuJoCo scenes (e.g. LiteReality output).

Two entry points (``ROADMAP.md`` §11, LiteReality-Agent: scan -> physics-ready scene):

- :func:`clean_scan` / :func:`add_scan`: a raw scan mesh (PLY/OBJ/GLB/STL from a phone, LiDAR or
  photogrammetry) -> merged duplicate vertices, degenerate and duplicate faces removed, small
  floating fragments dropped, holes filled, optional decimation, floor aligned to +Z (dominant
  area-weighted face normal), converted to metres. Returns a report of everything changed.
- :func:`scene_from_mjcf`: a MuJoCo MJCF scene (what LiteReality exports: articulated assets with
  mesh geoms) -> one Twin3D part per mesh geom, with the body/geom position and orientation chain
  applied. Primitive geoms (box, sphere, cylinder, capsule, plane) become simple meshes.

Requires ``trimesh`` (the ``geom`` extra). Point clouds without faces are rejected with a clear
message: surface reconstruction is not done here.

functions.name: clean_scan
functions.sig: (path_or_mesh, *, unit: str = 'm', min_component_fraction: float = 0.01, fill_holes: bool = True, target_faces: Optional[int] = None, align_floor: bool = True)
functions.doc: Clean a scan mesh. Returns ``(trimesh.Trimesh, ScanReport)`` in metres.

functions.name: add_scan
functions.sig: (scene: Scene, name: str, path_or_mesh, *, group: str = 'scan', **kw) -> ScanReport

functions.name: scene_from_mjcf
functions.sig: (path: str, *, title: Optional[str] = None, include_primitives: bool = True) -> Scene
functions.doc: One Twin3D part per geom of a MuJoCo scene, in world coordinates.

children.summary: Twin geometry from scans: cleaned scan meshes and MuJoCo scenes (e.g. LiteReality output).

children.name: pinneapple_twin3d.scene
children.doc:
Build and export a 3D digital-twin scene: parts, fields over time, sensors.

Export layout (one folder, static files, served by anything)::

    scene.json      manifest: parts, fields, time steps, sensors, units, provenance
    geometry.glb    all parts as glTF 2.0 binary meshes (opens in Blender, CAD viewers, three.js)
    fields.bin      float32 field values, part motions (position + quaternion per step) and per-step part
                    visibility, offsets listed in scene.json
    index.html,
    viewer.js       the bundled web viewer (see ``viewer/``), added by ``export(with_viewer=True)``

Geometry goes to glTF because it is the interchange format every 3D tool reads; fields stay
out of the glTF (a transient field is a (time, vertex) array, which glTF has no standard slot
for) and are addressed per part and per time step in the manifest. ``export(usd=True)`` also writes
OpenUSD (``usd.py``), including UsdPhysics rigid bodies / colliders / materials declared with
``add_physics`` and ``set_gravity``.

classes.name: PhysicsProps
classes.doc:
How a part takes part in a physics simulation (OpenUSD ``UsdPhysics``).

``rigid_body=False`` with ``collider=True`` is a static collider (floor,
wall). ``kinematic=True`` makes the body follow its recorded motion
(``Scene.add_motion``) instead of being integrated -- the right choice
when a twin replays measured or simulated poses.

classes.name: Scene
classes.sig: (title: str, *, length_unit: str = 'm', times: Sequence[float] | None = None, time_unit: str = 's', source: str = '')
classes.doc: A digital-twin scene. Add parts, fields and sensors, then ``export`` to a folder.

methods.name: add_part
methods.sig: (name: str, vertices, faces, *, group: str = '', color = (0.75, 0.77, 0.8)) -> Part

methods.name: add_field
methods.sig: (part: str, name: str, values, *, unit: str = '') -> None
methods.doc: Per-vertex field: shape (V,) for steady, (T, V) for transient (T = len(times)).

methods.name: add_motion
methods.doc:
Rigid motion of a part over the scene time steps: the part's vertices are in its own frame and are drawn
at ``positions[k] + rotate(quaternions[k], v)`` at step k. ``quaternions`` are (w, x, y, z).

methods.name: add_visibility
methods.doc: Whether a part is drawn at each scene time step (e.g. parts that appear or disappear in a sequence).

methods.name: set_step_labels
methods.doc: A caption per time step (what happens at that step), shown by the viewer next to the time.

methods.name: set_gravity
methods.doc: Declare a physics scene (USD ``PhysicsScene``) with this gravity vector in m/s^2.

methods.name: add_physics
methods.sig: (part: str, *, rigid_body: bool = True, collider: bool = True, kinematic: bool = False, mass: float | None = None, density: float | None = None, center_of_mass = None, approximation: str = 'convexHull', material: PhysicsMaterial | None = None, velocity = None, angular_velocity = None) -> PhysicsProps
methods.doc: Make a part a rigid body and/or collider for Omniverse / Isaac Sim / any UsdPhysics engine.

methods.name: add_sensor
methods.sig: (id: str, position, *, label: str = '', unit: str = '', quantity: str = '', series = None, envelope = None) -> Sensor

methods.name: to_studio
methods.doc:
This twin as a ``pp.viz`` Scene (fields at time step ``step``) for Blender renders, glTF/USD export or
the studio viewer; sensors are left out. ``up``: the twin's up axis ("z", engineering, or "y", e.g. a scene
built for the web viewer), mapped to the studio's z-up.

methods.name: render_blender
methods.sig: (out: str, *, step: int = -1, field: str | None = None, up: str = 'z', field_range = None, **kw) -> str
methods.doc: Blender Cycles render of the twin at time step ``step`` (``pip install bpy``), coloured by ``field``.

methods.name: render_blender_frames
methods.sig: (folder: str, steps: Sequence[int] | None = None, **kw) -> list[str]
methods.doc: One Blender render per time step (default: all) into ``folder``; returns the image paths.

methods.name: export
methods.sig: (folder: str, *, with_viewer: bool = True, usd: bool = False) -> str
methods.doc: Write scene.json + geometry.glb + fields.bin (+ viewer, + scene.usda with ``usd=True``).

children.summary: Build and export a 3D digital-twin scene: parts, fields over time, sensors.

children.name: pinneapple_twin3d.serve
children.doc: Serve an exported scene folder over HTTP (the viewer needs HTTP, not file://, to fetch its data).

functions.name: serve
functions.sig: (folder: str, port: int = 8765, *, host: str = '127.0.0.1', block: bool = True)
functions.doc: Serve ``folder`` at ``http://host:port/``. With ``block=False`` returns the running server.

children.summary: Serve an exported scene folder over HTTP (the viewer needs HTTP, not file://, to fetch its data).

children.name: pinneapple_twin3d.usd
children.doc:
Export a Twin3D scene as OpenUSD (``.usda`` text), for Omniverse / Isaac Sim / usdview.

Why USD next to glTF (``ROADMAP.md`` §11, NVIDIA GTC 2026 CAD -> sim -> twin thread): glTF has
no standard slot for a field that changes over time, USD does. Here every part is a ``Mesh``,
every field a per-vertex ``primvars:<name>`` whose values are **time samples** (one per scene
time step), and every sensor a ``Sphere`` with its series, unit and alarm envelope as custom
attributes. Provenance (title, source, units, real time values) goes into the layer metadata so
the meaning of the data survives the hand-off.

Physics (``UsdPhysics``): parts given ``Scene.add_physics`` become rigid bodies and/or colliders
(``PhysicsRigidBodyAPI``, ``PhysicsMassAPI``, ``PhysicsCollisionAPI``, ``PhysicsMeshCollisionAPI``),
with contact materials (``PhysicsMaterialAPI``) bound through ``material:binding:physics``;
``Scene.set_gravity`` adds a ``PhysicsScene``. Recorded rigid motion (``Scene.add_motion``) is written
as time-sampled ``xformOp:translate`` / ``xformOp:orient`` -- with ``kinematic=True`` the body replays
it, so the same file opens as a playback in usdview and as a live scene in Omniverse / Isaac Sim.

Written as plain text: no ``pxr`` dependency to export. ``usd-core`` (``pip install usd-core``)
can open the result; the tests use it when available.
children.summary: Export a Twin3D scene as OpenUSD (.usda text), for Omniverse / Isaac Sim / usdview.

pinneapple_twin3d.wear.build
children.doc: WearDataset -> Scene (3D viewer) + hub contract + forecast/optimizer report.

functions.sig: (ds: WearDataset, folder: str, *, cfg: Optional[OptimizerConfig] = None, usd: bool = False, **fit_kw) -> str

children.name: pinneapple_twin3d.wear.calibrate
children.doc:
Calibrate the optimizer's assumptions from the plant's own records.

What the data can and cannot tell:

=====================  ===========================================  =========================================
parameter              estimated from                               needs
=====================  ===========================================  =========================================
setup_hours,           stop log: ``duration = setup + per_zone * n``  >= 3 stops, >= 2 different zone counts
hours_per_zone
cost_per_hour,         stop log with a cost: ``cost = c_h*duration     >= 4 stops with cost
cost_per_zone          + c_z*n_zones``
recovery_frac          the dataset itself: size of the wear drop      >= 20 repaired cells
                       at each detected repair / usable thickness
breach_cost_per_x,     **business inputs** (what a heat beyond the    nothing: never inferred
safety_margin, ...     limit costs, how much margin you want)
=====================  ===========================================  =========================================

Every parameter is reported with its source (``calibrated`` / ``default`` / ``business input``), the sample size and
the standard error where one exists; a fit that gives a negative time or cost is rejected and the default is kept.

functions.name: estimate_recovery
functions.doc: Median fraction of the usable thickness restored per repaired cell, and the number of cells used.

functions.name: calibrate
functions.sig: (stops: Sequence[StopRecord] = (), ds: Optional[WearDataset] = None, base: Optional[OptimizerConfig] = None) -> Calibration

children.summary: Calibrate the optimizer's assumptions from the plant's own records.

children.name: pinneapple_twin3d.wear.forecast
children.doc:
Remaining-life forecast per cell: the model of the reference twins, plus confidence.

For each cell, residual thickness ``e0 - wear`` is fitted by least squares against ``x`` over the
trailing window (``win_x`` units of x, widened to at least ``min_pts`` readings when readings are sparse)
and the fit stops at a *repair* (a drop of wear larger than ``repair_drop`` (8 %) of the usable thickness).
``remaining = (residual - emin) / -slope``; cells already at/below the limit have ``remaining = 0``
(the rate is still estimated); flat or growing thickness gives ``inf``.

It is a **linear extrapolation**: it cannot anticipate a change of regime. ``confidence`` only grades the
quality of the fit (points and R^2), it is not a probability. ``remaining_lo/hi`` is a 90 % Student-t
interval on the slope (n >= 3), propagated to the remaining life: a *fit* uncertainty, not a prediction interval
for regime changes.

functions.name: t90
functions.doc: Student-t 0.95 quantile (90 % two-sided interval) for ``df`` degrees of freedom (array ok).

functions.name: fit_zone
functions.sig: (ds: WearDataset, zone: str, s: int, *, win_x: float = DEFAULT_WIN_X, min_pts: int = 8, repair_drop: float = 0.08) -> CellFit

functions.name: forecast
functions.sig: (ds: WearDataset, s: Optional[int] = None, **kw) -> Dict[str, ZoneForecast]

functions.name: forecast_history
functions.doc: Minimum predicted remaining life recomputed at every reading (how the forecast evolved).

functions.name: backtest
functions.doc: Compare past predictions of 'x when the first cell hits the limit' with what happened.

children.summary: Remaining-life forecast per cell: the model of the reference twins, plus confidence.

children.name: pinneapple_twin3d.wear.geometry
children.doc:
Cell meshes for surfaces of revolution.

Each cell gets its own 4 vertices (two triangles), so a *per-cell* value becomes a per-vertex field with
no interpolation: what the viewer colours is exactly the cell's measurement. Cell ``(i, j)`` (row i along
the profile, sector j around the axis) owns vertices ``4*(i*M + j) .. +3``.

Convention (same as the reference apps): y is up, ``x = r cos(th)``, ``z = -r sin(th)``, so angles run
counter-clockwise seen from above; row 0 is the first profile point.

functions.name: sample_profile
functions.doc: (n_rows + 1, 2) points (r, y) equally spaced in arc length along the polyline.

functions.name: cell_mesh
functions.doc: Vertices (N*M*4, 3) and faces (N*M*2, 3) of the zone, one quad per cell.

functions.name: cell_to_vertex
functions.doc: Per-cell values (..., N, M) -> per-vertex (..., N*M*4) following ``cell_mesh``'s ordering.

functions.name: cell_centers
functions.doc: (N, M, 3) world position of each cell centre (used to place sensors / hotspots).

children.summary: Cell meshes for surfaces of revolution.

children.name: pinneapple_twin3d.wear.model
children.doc:
Data model of a wear twin: vessel spec (geometry + zones) and the wear dataset.

A *zone* is a surface of revolution: a profile polyline ``(r, y)`` swept around the vertical axis
and cut into ``n_rows x n_sectors`` cells. That single abstraction covers a cylindrical wall, a cone,
a flat or dished floor (profile along r at fixed y), and an off-axis leg (``center``), which is how
the four reference refractory twins (steel ladle, pig-iron ladle, BOF, RH degasser) are described.

The dataset is the *contract* shared with the web hub of the reference suite
(``to_contract`` / ``from_contract``): measurements are wear depth per cell and per reading ``x``
(heat number, days, ...), never a model output unless ``origin`` says so.

classes.name: WearDataset
classes.doc: Wear depth [mm] per zone: ``wear[zone]`` has shape (T, rows, sectors); NaN = no reading.

children.summary: Data model of a wear twin: vessel spec (geometry + zones) and the wear dataset.

children.name: pinneapple_twin3d.wear.optimize
children.doc:
Maintenance (gunning / repair) scheduling over the forecast. Decision support only.

Port of ``digital-solutions/shared/optimizer.js`` so both sides give the same numbers.

Model (explicit and auditable):
* each zone has a ``deadline`` (x until its critical cell reaches the minimum thickness; 0 = already there);
* an intervention at ``T`` restores ``recovery_frac`` of the usable thickness, capped at the design
  thickness: ``new_deadline = T + min(margin(T) + ext, life_full)``, ``ext = recovery_frac * life_full``;
* several zones can be served in one stop (one setup cost);
* *breach* = x operated with some zone beyond its limit.

Three policies are simulated: run-to-limit (``reactive``), fixed calendar (``fixed``) and ``predictive``
grouped stops (greedy with a search over the grouping window). The recommendation is the cheapest
policy with no breach (or, if none, the one with the least breach).

functions.name: simulate
functions.sig: (zs: Sequence[ZoneState], stops: Sequence[dict], cfg: OptimizerConfig) -> dict

functions.name: optimize
functions.sig: (forecasts: Dict[str, ZoneForecast] | Sequence[ZoneForecast], cfg: Optional[OptimizerConfig] = None) -> OptimizationResult

children.summary: Maintenance (gunning / repair) scheduling over the forecast.

children.name: pinneapple_twin3d.wear.presets
children.doc:
The four reference use cases as specs: steel ladle, pig-iron ladle, BOF converter, RH degasser.

Geometry is derived from the proportions published in the reference twins (a ~230 t steel ladle, ~300 t
pig-iron ladle, ~300 t BOF, RH snorkel vessel); it is *indicative*, not a drawing of a specific plant.
Replace dimensions with the plant's drawings for a real project - nothing else changes.

``get(key)`` returns ``(spec, hotspots)``; hot spots are only used for the synthetic demonstration.

functions.name: fill_level
functions.sig: (rin, y0, y1, rho, mass, n = 300) -> float
functions.doc: Bath level for ``mass`` [t] in a vessel of inner radius ``rin(y)`` (frustum integration).

functions.name: smelting_reduction_reactor
functions.doc:
Generic smelting-reduction shaft reactor: shaft, tuyere zone, crucible, hearth.

Sector 0 is the tap hole; the tuyeres sit between tap holes, evenly spaced. Wear limit 300 mm of a 450 mm lining.

children.summary: The four reference use cases as specs: steel ladle, pig-iron ladle, BOF converter, RH degasser.

children.name: pinneapple_twin3d.wear.synthetic
children.doc:
Synthetic wear campaigns: explicit hot spots + growth law + repairs. Always labelled SYNTHETIC.

Use it to demonstrate a twin before real thickness data exists. It is *not* a physical model: the hot
spots encode where the process is known to attack the lining (slag line, jet impact, ...), the amplitudes
are illustrative.

functions.name: base_pattern
functions.sig: (spec: VesselSpec, hotspots: Sequence[HotSpot], base: float) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]

functions.name: synthetic_campaign
functions.sig: (spec: VesselSpec, hotspots: Sequence[HotSpot], *, n_readings: int = 41, x_max: float = 120.0, growth_power: float = 1.0, base: float = 0.2, noise: float = 0.01, seed: int = 0, repairs: Sequence[float] = (), repair_zones: Sequence[str] = (), repair_gain: float = 0.4) -> WearDataset
functions.doc:
``noise`` is the sigma of additive measurement noise as a fraction of the usable thickness.
Wear grows as ``(x/x_max)**growth_power`` towards ``pattern * usable``; at each ``repairs`` x the
wear of ``repair_zones`` drops by ``repair_gain`` of its value (gunning), then resumes.

children.summary: Synthetic wear campaigns: explicit hot spots + growth law + repairs.

children.doc:
Generator of 3D wear (refractory / liner / pipe) digital twins from a spec.

    from pinneapple_twin3d.wear import presets, synthetic_campaign, export_wear_twin
    spec, hotspots = presets.get("bof")
    ds = synthetic_campaign(spec, hotspots)          # clearly labelled synthetic
    export_wear_twin(ds, "out/bof"); serve("out/bof")

Pipeline: ``VesselSpec`` -> ``WearDataset`` -> ``forecast`` -> ``optimize`` -> ``Scene`` (viewer) + report.
children.summary: Generator of 3D wear (refractory / liner / pipe) digital twins from a spec.

doc:
3D digital-twin visualization: build a scene in Python, open it in the bundled web viewer.

    from pinneapple_twin3d import Scene, serve
    sc = Scene("CFD-04 bend", times=[0, 1, 2], time_unit="year")
    sc.add_trimesh("bend", trimesh.load("bend.stl"), group="pipe")
    sc.add_field("bend", "wear_depth", wear_TxV, unit="mm")
    sc.add_sensor("PT-101", (0.1, 0.0, 0.2), unit="bar", series=[4.1, 4.0, 3.8], envelope=(3.5, 5.0))
    sc.export("out/twin", usd=True)  # scene.json + geometry.glb + fields.bin + viewer (+ scene.usda)
    serve("out/twin")              # http://localhost:8765/  (add ?live=ws://... for live sensors)

Also: ``pinneapple_twin3d.openfoam.scene_from_case`` (OpenFOAM wall patches + per-face values over
time, e.g. erosion maps), ``pinneapple_twin3d.usd.export_usd`` (OpenUSD with time-sampled fields)
and ``pinneapple_twin3d.demo.pipe_bend_scene`` (try the viewer without data).

Wear twins (refractory / liner): ``pinneapple_twin3d.wear`` builds a twin from a spec (see
``docs/guides/recreate_a_wear_twin.md``).

Decision D1 in docs/dev/PEDIDOS_2026-09-24.md: the viewer lives in the library so that
PINNeAPPle-CFD (3D wear over time), PINNeAPPle-apps and pinneapple_systems.digital_twin all
reuse it.
